ideas.pitch: A real-time women safety navigation web app that scores walking routes based on street lighting density, crowd reports, and historical incident heatmaps using spatial analysis.
ideas.title: AegisRoute
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the Women Safety domain which is a primary focus area for the IEEE WIE judges, moving beyond generic panic buttons to predictive route optimization.

ideas.pitch: An offline-first mobile web app for rural farmers that diagnoses crop diseases from smartphone leaf photos and forecasts local market price trends using lightweight models.
ideas.title: AgriYield-ML
ideas.why_it_could_win: Tailored for the Agriculture & Rural Innovation domain by addressing the dual pain points of crop loss and lack of transparent market pricing for smallholders.

ideas.pitch: An enterprise AI agent that automatically audits health insurance claim rejections against hospital discharge summaries and policy documents to generate point-by-point appeal letters.
ideas.title: MediClaim Audit Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages complex document parsing and structured legal/medical reasoning, aligning with the winning formula of solving painful institutional friction found in similar hackathons.

ideas.pitch: A carbon credit and supply chain tracking dashboard for rural agricultural co-operatives producing biochar, ensuring verified environmental impact data for sustainable tech buyers.
ideas.title: BioCharbon Tracking
ideas.why_it_could_win: Bridges Sustainable Technology and Agriculture & Rural Innovation by providing transparent, verifiable impact metrics that corporate ESG judges look for.

ideas.pitch: An automated micro-loan underwriting and fraud detection platform tailored for rural self-help groups, combining alternative behavioral data with explainable credit scoring.
ideas.title: MicroGuard FinTech
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the FinTech Innovation domain with a strong social impact angle, making financial services safer and more accessible for underserved rural communities.
